# Intake Brief: Automated Balancing

> **Headline:** Turn the existing same-seed evaluation harness into an
> automated-balancing framework that simulates hundreds of deterministic bot
> games against the real balance data files and reports full statistics, so
> tuning is driven by evidence instead of intuition.

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** epic · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Balancing the game is currently a manual, point-in-time activity: a designer
edits `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` / `ship-config.csv` / `difficulty-curves.csv`,
reloads, watches a run, and guesses. The pieces to do better already exist — a
deterministic headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`), a metric/A-B layer
(`src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`), and a telemetry schema that already records
minerals, upgrades (`choice_selected`), kills (`enemy_killed`) and pickups —
but the arena is **not config-driven** (it hardcodes `scout/diver/phaser`, a
fixed fire cadence and radius), the metric layer does **not** aggregate
per-upgrade or per-archetype statistics, and there is no way to run a **batch
of hundreds of games** and read its aggregated distribution. We need a
framework that simulates many bot games, collects full balance statistics, and
reports them so balance can be tuned from evidence rather than intuition.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want to run hundreds of bot games
  after changing a balance value and get a statistical report (minerals,
  upgrades, kills, survival, wave reached), so I can see whether the change
  improved or hurt play before shipping it.
- **As the bot maintainer**, I want the simulated scenario to read the real
  balance data files, so a run reflects the tuning I just made (not a
  hardcoded copy).
- **As a producer**, I want a stable, reproducible artifact per batch, so a
  balance change can be reviewed and compared over time.
- **As a downstream consumer** (the human-play stats and periodic
  human-experience validation work items), I want one shared balance-statistics
  schema, so bot and human measurements are directly comparable.

## Acceptance criteria
- **Config-driven simulation.** A headless run consumes the real balance data (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/data/ship-config.csv`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` and/or the shared wave sequencer) through the existing config loaders, with no divergent copy of enemy/ship/wave stats. A test demonstrates that changing a CSV value changes the simulated outcome (e.g. enemy health/`shotProbability`).
- **Batch runner.** A documented command runs at least ~100 deterministic bot games (seeds × policy) in one invocation and completes in a practical time on a dev machine, emitting raw telemetry plus an aggregated report. Same seed + config + policy yields a byte-identical report.
- **Full balance statistics.** The report captures, per run and aggregated, at minimum: minerals collected, upgrades selected (per upgrade/choice id), enemies killed **per archetype**, asteroids destroyed, power-ups collected, avoidable hits, survival time, and wave/level reached — with distribution summaries (count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev) across games.
- **Human-readable + machine-readable output.** The batch writes stable JSON artifacts and prints (or writes) a human-readable balance summary; the statistics schema is versioned and shared, not duplicated.
- **Tests.** Pure aggregation, determinism and the config-driven arena are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
## Constraints

- **Determinism (preserve AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4 AC5).** Every run derives from a
  seed; no wall clock; the batch report is reproducible byte-for-byte.
- **Dev/eval only.** No production runtime impact and no addition to the
  shipped gameplay path; `src/ai/eval/` stays pure (no I/O, no wall clock);
  filesystem work stays in the Node shell (`scripts/evaluate.mjs`).
- **Single source of truth.** The arena must consume the shared config
  loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` / `enemyConfig.ts` /
  `difficultySequencer.ts`), never a second copy of enemy or ship stats.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The arena is a dev tool (like the gyms); any shared
  gameplay behaviour it exercises must come from the shared core
  (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/utils/movementModel.ts`), never a divergent copy.
- **No PII.** Reuse the existing telemetry schema and redaction policy.
- **Bounded resources.** Hundreds of runs must not exhaust memory; keep the
  per-run footprint small and stream/aggregate incrementally where possible.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — deterministic headless arena; hardcoded
  `['scout','diver','phaser']`, fixed `ENEMY_FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS`,
  `HOSTILE_RADIUS`, and `SHIP_CONFIG`; not config-driven.
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — `MetricPoint`/`MetricAggregate` with score,
  survival, minerals-per-minute, power-ups, enemies/asteroids destroyed,
  avoidable hits, input cadence, dodge rate; **no per-upgrade or per-archetype
  breakdown and no percentile distribution**.
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` / `cli.ts` / `report.ts` — single/A-B evaluation over
  a small seed list (`--seeds N`, default 3); reports stored as JSON/JSONL.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — Node shell (Vite SSR module loader, file I/O).
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — documents the existing harness.
- `src/data/*.csv` + `src/core/configStore.ts` — the real, editable balance
  data and its loader.
- Telemetry already emits `enemy_killed {archetype,x,y}`, `pickup {kind,id}`,
  `mineral_collected {total}`, `choice_selected {index,id}`, `wave_*`,
  `level_cleared`.

## Desired change

Turn the eval harness into an automated-balancing framework:

1. Make the headless arena **config-driven** from the real balance data.
2. Add a **batch runner** for hundreds of deterministic games.
3. Extend the metric layer with the **full balance-statistics schema** and
   distribution summaries (per-upgrade, per-archetype, wave reached, etc.).
4. Emit **JSON + human-readable** balance reports; version the schema so human
   and periodic-validation consumers can share it.
5. Document how to run a batch and interpret the report; cover it with tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — make the arena consume real enemy/ship/wave data.
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — add balance-statistics extraction + distributions.
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — extend statistics/report types (versioned schema).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — include the new statistics and batch summary.
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — batch runner over many games/seeds.
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` and `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — CLI flags for batch size,
  statistics output and report.
- `src/ai/eval/index.ts` — public surface for the shared statistics schema.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` / `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` /
  `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — consumed as the single source of truth.
- `src/ai/eval/*.test.ts` — tests for aggregation, determinism, config-driven
  behaviour.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` (and/or a new `docs/BALANCING.md`) — how to run a batch
  and read the report.

## Risks, assumptions and mitigations

- **Assumption:** the "reasonably accurate human-like" bot is the `competent`
  policy; the batch runner defaults to it.
- **Assumption:** "hundreds of games" means roughly 100–1000 deterministic
  runs (seeds × policies) per batch.
- **Fidelity risk:** the headless arena is a simplification, so bot balance
  stats may not match the shipped game. *Mitigation:* make it config-driven,
  document the fidelity boundary, and pair it with the human-play statistics
  and periodic human-experience validation items below.
- **Environment risk:** loading CSV-backed config under Node/Vite SSR may need
  verification. *Mitigation:* prototype config loading first (spike within the
  item) before building the statistics layer on top.
- **Scope-creep risk:** human-play collection and periodic human-experience
  validation are **separate work items** (below) — do not fold them into this
  epic. Any further opportunities get their own linked item.

## Related work

- **Same-seed evaluation harness: metrics, A/B, side-by-side** (AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4) — the foundation this builds on.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ) — recording/analysis path reused for human stats.
- **Telemetry: per-tick integration with no-op contract** (AH-0MUZQEDW9002KHRN) and the telemetry framework (AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO).
- **Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling** (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP) — balance-rule consumer.
- **Tune enemy balance: reduce scout durability and tank firing** (AH-0MULW9HNC001GVCY) — the manual pass this automates.
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — shares the statistics schema.
- **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — depends on this epic.
- **Reduce bullet speed of enemies** (AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ) — a completed tuning pass on `enemy-configs.csv` (bulletSpeed/lifetime) that this framework would measure instead of eyeballing.
- **Write tests for new game scenes and systems** (AH-0MU732AJW005RTG1) — precedent for the test expectations on the new stats layer.
- Docs: `docs/EVALUATION.md`, `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Integration/scope.** How should this relate to the existing same-seed harness?
  - **Answer (operator):** A — extend the existing harness (`src/ai/eval/`, `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`) with a batch/statistics layer. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Fidelity / what gets simulated.** What should the simulation actually run?
  - **Answer (operator):** A — extend the existing headless arena to be config-driven from `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv` and `ship-config.csv`, so tuning edits are measurable. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Statistics and output.** Which statistic set/format?
  - **Answer (operator):** A — full stats (minerals, per-upgrade choice counts, per-archetype kills, wave/level reached, survival-time distribution, avoidable hits) as per-seed + aggregate distributions, output as JSON artifacts and a human-readable report. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 — Human player data.** Could the same data be collected from human player games?
  - **Answer (operator):** Yes — create a **high-priority** work item to collect the same data in human player games, **dev mode only**. Created as **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5 — Periodic human-experience validation.** Should there be a check against the intended experience?
  - **Answer (operator):** Yes — create another work item, **dependent on both** this framework and the human-play stats item, to periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience. Created as **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775), with dependency edges to AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW and AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX** – Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support (completed)
- **AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L** – Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids (completed)
- **AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ** – Reduce bullet speed of enemies (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muy08xld009k4w4, ac5, acceptance, accurate, activity (+354 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muwz5gst003nmfq, 0mv29xq0h009p9wp, ac5, accurate, activity (+320 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muwz5gst003nmfq, 0mv29xq0h009p9wp, ac5, actually, add (+290 more)

---

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-14: Decomposed into 6 features (schema+aggregation, config-driven arena, batch runner, report+CLI, docs, acceptance verification). Coverage review verified at 100% (proceed). Note: tree-coverage auto-close placeholder children were removed and replaced with explicit 'Covers epic ACn' bullets.

# Bot steering model to consume live ShipConfig thruster values — Intake Brief

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** task (model plumbing/refactor, no new user-facing capability)

## Problem statement

The demo/competent bot's steering and forward model use hard-coded thruster
constants (`playerSpeed: 175`, `frictionDeceleration: 100`, and no reverse
values at all) instead of the player ship's live `ShipConfig`, so a change to
the player's thruster configuration is never picked up by the bot. This makes
the demo bot physically wrong against a tuned ship (wrong stopping distances,
wrong assumed cruise speed, and no representation of the reverse thruster's
acceleration/max speed).

## Users

- **Player watching the attract/demo** — expects the bot to fly the *same ship
  physics* the player configured, so the demo is a faithful preview of the
  game.
- **Developer / designer tuning ship config** — wants the demo bot to react
  correctly when thruster values are edited, so tuning can be validated
  against a skilled pilot.

Example user stories:

- As a player who tuned high friction, the bot stops within the predicted
  margin instead of sliding past, so the demo looks skilled with my ship.
- As a designer editing `frictionDeceleration`/`maxSpeed`, the demo bot's
  steering and stopping behaviour tracks the change without code edits, so I
  can validate tuning in a gym/run.
- As a player who disabled or re-tuned the reverse thruster, the bot's
  reverse braking uses my configured acceleration and speed cap, so the demo
  never contradicts the handling I experience.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Live thruster config in the snapshot.** `BotSnapshot` carries the
   player's live thruster configuration — forward `thrustAcceleration`,
   `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration`, and reverse `enabled` /
   `reverseAcceleration` / `reverseMaxSpeed` — sourced from the live
   `Player`/`ShipConfig` via `buildBotSnapshot`, not from tunables. The
   existing demo path (`PlayScene._advanceDemoBot` → `buildBotSnapshot(this)`)
   picks it up automatically with no hard-coded physics in the decision layer.
2. **AC2 — Steering/forward model consumes live values.** The steering
   candidate prediction (`evaluateDirection` player-speed term) and the
   forward-model thrust decision (`mayThrust` friction stopping distance)
   use the snapshot's live values; the tunables `playerSpeed` /
   `frictionDeceleration` are demoted to **defaults/overrides** (fallback when
   the snapshot carries no config, and overridable via GymBotTuning), never
   authoritative. **Precedence (pending producer confirmation): live
   ShipConfig wins for physics terms when present (option (a)); explicit gym
   overrides otherwise.**
3. **AC3 — Reverse thrust represented in the model.** Reverse braking is gated
   and modelled with the live reverse values: `asteroidsReverseEnabled`
   (already respected at snapshot level), `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration`
   and `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` feed the reverse forward-model (brake
   distance under reverse acceleration and/or reverse speed cap) instead of
   being absent. The existing `mayReverse` tuning gates
   (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`) remain tunables.
4. **AC4 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour change is applied consistently to
   the shipped game (`PlayScene` + shared core) and the gym scenes that
   exercise the bot (e.g. `GymBotTuning`), sharing the same snapshot/steering
   code — no divergent copy.
5. **AC5 — Testing & validation.** Unit tests cover (a) a custom thruster
   config changing the bot's steering/stopping/reverse decisions vs the
   defaults, and (b) the fallback path with no config in the snapshot
   (unchanged behaviour vs today). At least one test pins the pure decision
   layer consuming live values. **Full project test suite must pass with the
   new changes.**
6. **AC6 — Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and
   any relevant wiki/docs entries.

## Constraints

- The decision layer stays **pure and deterministic** — the snapshot is the
  only runtime input; no reading ship state from inside steering functions.
- Behaviour must be applied consistently to gyms and game (repo-wide
  duplicate-body guard + gym-parity docs assertion enforce this).
- Tunables must remain overridable (persisted `GymBotTuning` config and its
  `toCompetentOverrides` mapping) — overrides still win over live config
  where they exist, matching the current tuning seam.
- `assumedBulletSpeed` (enemy-bullet speed for fire-tell prediction) and
  `firePredictionHorizon` are **out of scope** — they model enemy bullets, not
  the player's ship, and stay tunables.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` hard-codes `playerSpeed: 175` and
  `frictionDeceleration: 100`; reverse braking has tuning gates
  (`reverseBrakeEnabled`, `reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`)
  but **no** reverse acceleration/max-speed in the model.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` uses `t.playerSpeed` in
  `evaluateDirection` (candidate-speed prediction) and
  `t.frictionDeceleration` in `mayThrust` (stopping distance); `mayReverse`
  gates on tunables only.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` exposes only position/velocity on `BotPlayer`
  (`x, y, vx, vy`) plus a snapshot-level `reverseEnabled` boolean; there is no
  thruster-physics field.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` holds the fleet thruster values in
  `_baseConfig`/`_config` (`thrust`, `maxSpeed`, `friction`, `reverseEnabled`,
  `reverseAcceleration`, `reverseMaxSpeed`) but exposes only
  `getRotationConfig()` and `isReverseEnabled()` publicly — no getter for the
  thruster physics.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_advanceDemoBot` already routes
  `buildBotSnapshot(this)` into the brain, so a snapshot change flows through
  automatically.

## Desired change

- Add thruster-physics fields to `BotPlayer` (or a nested `thruster` object)
  in `botSnapshot.ts`, populated from a new Player getter
  (e.g. `getThrusterConfig()` returning forward thrust/max speed/friction and
  reverse enabled/acceleration/max speed — mirroring `getRotationConfig`).
- In `steering.ts`, read live values from the snapshot/world for the
  candidate-speed term and the friction/reverse stopping model, falling back
  to the (renamed/documented as defaults) tunables when absent.
- Update `tunables.ts` defaults and doc comments to mark
  `playerSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration` (and any new reverse physics defaults)
  as fallback defaults + tuning overrides, not the ship's truth.
- Keep `update`-seam behaviour identical when no config is present (fallback
  equals today's constants).

## Key Files

- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — Add live thruster config to the snapshot and `BotPlayer`; update the `BotSnapshotScene`/`BotPlayerSource` structural seams.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — New public getter for thruster physics (forward + reverse), mirroring `getRotationConfig()`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection`, `mayThrust`, `mayReverse` consume live values with tunable fallback.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — Demote physics constants to defaults/overrides; doc updates.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — Ensure `BotWorld.player` carries the config (it derives from the snapshot), and any reverse forward-model terms.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Demo path (already wired via `buildBotSnapshot`); verify no other hard-coded thruster use in the bot seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — Parity: verify the tuning overrides still win over live config.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`, `competentBot.test.ts`, and `src/ai/botSnapshot` builder tests.
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5 — Bot to use the reverse thrusters** (parent; AC4 of
  that item explicitly defers "numeric customisation of the bot's *model* to
  live thruster values" to this item).
- **AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 — Overuse of the reverse thrusters** (reverse reserved
  for trouble/correction — this item must preserve those semantics).
- **AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0 — Gym scene for AI bot tuning** (`GymBotTuning`,
  persisted tunables seam).
- **AH-0MV2JT18K006YU35 — Reverse intent and enable-flag plumbing** (the
  `reverseEnabled` snapshot field this item extends with numeric values).
- **AH-0MV13LXOR001X15X — Config fields for the reverse thruster** (source of
  the `asteroidsReverse*` `ShipConfig` fields this item consumes).
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md** (AC4
  parity convention and the repo-wide duplicate-body guard that enforces it).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Fallback equivalence must be exact.** With the default ship config
  (`MAX_SPEED=175`, `FRICTION_DECELERATION=100` in `constants.ts`) the
  fallback values match today's tunables (`playerSpeed: 175`,
  `frictionDeceleration: 100`) exactly, so a ship running defaults must behave
  bit-for-bit as today. Any regression here is invisible-but-harmful to the
  demo bot.
- **Tuning-seam precedence (scope tension).** The tuning gym
  (`tuningFields.ts`) exposes `playerSpeed` and `frictionDeceleration` as
  sliders. If live `ShipConfig` becomes authoritative for physics terms, those
  two sliders become no-ops whenever a ship config is present (the live game
  always has one). Mitigation: record the expected precedence in the ACs
  (option (a) live-wins recommended) and flag the now-inert sliders as a
  follow-up work item rather than expanding scope here.
- **Assumption — `maxSpeed` is the live proxy for the candidate-speed term.**
  `playerSpeed` (assumed cruise speed for candidate-direction prediction)
  maps to `ShipConfig.maxSpeed`; the default value (175) already equals the
  tunable, so this is behaviour-preserving at defaults. If the intent were a
  *fraction* of max speed (cruise < cap), note that the current 175 is the
  full cap — the implementer should keep the default-equivalence property.
- **Scope-creep guard.** `assumedBulletSpeed` / `firePredictionHorizon`
  (enemy-bullet modelling) and rotation physics (already live via
  `getRotationConfig`, AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98) are out of scope; any further
  tuning-surface changes (e.g. deprecating sliders) are recorded as linked
  work items, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required — the seed context (item description, parent
AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5 AC4 note, and the competent-bot framework docs) plus repo
evidence (`tunables.ts`, `steering.ts`, `botSnapshot.ts`, `Player.ts`,
`configTypes.ts`) were sufficient to draft the brief.

- Q: "Which `ShipConfig` values feed the bot model?" — Answer (research):
  `thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration`,
  `asteroidsReverseEnabled`, `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration`,
  `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` (see `src/core/configTypes.ts`). Source: repo
  inspection (Player `_baseConfig` mapping, `getRotationConfig()` precedent).
- Q: "Do `playerSpeed` / `frictionDeceleration` disappear?" — Answer
  (research, from the item description): no — they become **defaults /
  overrides** (fallback for absence, overridable via GymBotTuning), never
  authoritative. Source: item description line "Update tunables to be
  defaults/overrides rather than authoritative values."
- Q: "Is `assumedBulletSpeed` (enemy-bullet speed) in scope?" — Answer
  (research): no — it models enemy bullets, not the player's ship. Source:
  `steering.ts` (fire-tell lead) and `worldModel.ts`
  (`assumedBulletSpeed`). Recorded as an out-of-scope constraint.
- Q: "When live ShipConfig is present, what wins for `playerSpeed` /
  `frictionDeceleration` (also exposed as tuning-gym sliders)?" — Answer
  (producer reply pending): **option (a) live config wins for physics terms**
  is recommended (matches "live values picked up automatically"); the gym
  sliders become fallback-only and should be flagged as inert in a follow-up.
  Source: pending producer response to the clarifying question.
- OPEN QUESTION (for the producer): Should the reverse forward-model compute a
  full reverse-assisted braking distance (speed → 0 under
  `reverseAcceleration`, capped by `reverseMaxSpeed`) or only clamp the
  modeled reverse speed cap and keep the friction-based gate? The draft keeps
  the existing gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`)
  and leaves the precise reverse physics formula to the implementer, but
  confirms the live numbers must be consumed (AC3).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC** – Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust) (completed)
- **AH-0MTECNKPC00954HH** – Test: Per-scene — player/combat assertions + regression (completed)
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** – Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic that seeks power-ups and minerals and dodges fire patterns (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv1dusm2005hl98, absent, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+336 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv1dusm2005hl98, absent, ac1, ac3, ac4 (+316 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, absent, ac1, ac3, ac4 (+283 more)

# Tests: recharge tick, auto-defence resolver, parity

## Goal

Verify the recharge wiring through the shared tick path, the finite-pool automatic-defence resolver, and game↔gym parity before implementing the wiring (test-first; drives the wiring implementation feature).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` advances the injected level store's recharge timers so depleted Phase Shift/Teleport pools recover over time.
- `selectAutoDefence` with finite capped pools: the greater available count wins, an exact tie uses the injected-RNG 50/50, `null` when both pools are empty, and partial (mid-recharge) pools order exactly per the parent resolver rule — with no unbounded/permanent-Infinity branch.
- `updateDanger` spends a defence only when the selected pool is non-empty; an empty pool contributes zero available count.
- Scene parity: the recharge advance runs through the shared registry tick consumed by PlayScene, GymFormationScene and GymPowerUpsCombat; the duplicate-body guard / equivalence suite still passes (gym ↔ game parity).
- HUD-facing accessors (`phaseCharges()`, `teleportStacks()`, `phaseRechargeTime()`, `teleportRechargeTime()`) report recharge-aware values.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (tick-advances-recharge, finite-pool resolver, updateDanger) and the parity suites (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`) where the recharge path is exercised.
- No production code changes in this item (test-first) — red until the wiring implementation lands.

## Dependencies

- Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore (the engine must exist to tick).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/effects.test.ts
- src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts

# Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence

## Goal

Advance the store's recharge timers from the shared registry tick (the one path every scene consumes, guaranteeing parity) and convert the automatic-defence resolver from the old unlimited-permanent model to finite capped pools.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` advances the injected store's recharge timers (shared tick path → identical behaviour in the game and every gym).
- `selectAutoDefence` no longer treats any pool as unbounded: both Phase Shift and Teleport are finite pools capped at 3; ordering by greater available count and the exact-tie RNG branch are unchanged; the permanent-Phase-Shift-Infinity branch is removed.
- `updateDanger` selects a defence only when the pool is non-empty (an empty pool contributes zero available count); the shared re-arm governor and `PHASE_REARM_COOLDOWN` (0.5 s) are unchanged.
- Registry accessors (`phaseCharges()`, `teleportStacks()`, `phaseRechargeTime()`, `teleportRechargeTime()`) reflect recharge state for the HUD.
- No gameplay divergence between the game and the gyms (shared registry tick + shared resolver, duplicate-body guard green).

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/powerups/effects.ts`: tick wiring, `selectAutoDefence` signature/body (drop the permanent-Infinity semantics), HUD accessors, header docs.
- `CombatScene._updateAutoDefence` and the scene tick sites consume the registry unchanged (verify no edits needed).

## Dependencies

- Tests: recharge tick, auto-defence resolver, parity (test-first).
- Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore.

## Key Files

- src/powerups/effects.ts

Enforce R1–R3 as hard constraints in sequencer composition (parent AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP, F3; covers AC2).

## Goal
Make src/core/difficultySequencer.ts never produce a generated (curve/dynamic) wave that violates the balance rules, consuming the shared rule module (AH-0MV84TE7O006HI3R) — no duplicated rule logic.

## Context
- The sequencer composes waves greedily from candidate groups using enemyDifficulty; it has a per-level archetype cap (MAX_ARCHETYPE_PER_LEVEL) as a precedent for composition constraints (AH-0MV2SGIX5005PFJT).
- R1 is position-dependent (opening waves), which the pure sequencer cannot know. R1 is enforced by constraining the candidate pool the campaign builder supplies (F4); the sequencer enforces R2 and R3 generically and validates its output with the shared validator, so the rules remain a single source of truth. Pass an explicit rule/context through SequencerOptions (e.g. allow the caller to supply R1-allowed movement classes) so enforcement still uses the shared module.
- Rules win over exact target match: the sequencer minimises difficulty error within the rule-constrained candidate space.

## Acceptance Criteria
- difficultySequencer imports and applies the shared rules from src/core/waveBalance.ts — no re-implemented rule logic.
- For the default candidate pool and a range of target curves (including single-wave, multi-wave, low/high targets), unit tests prove no generated wave violates R2 or R3, and that R1-constrained pools produce only formation/diver groups.
- Firing waves include at least one effective-contact group (R3); no-fire waves are not forced to add a contact group (producer Q1).
- Where rules bind, the composed wave still returns a playable result (never empty) and the remaining difficulty error is the minimum available within the constrained space.
- Existing sequencer tests (difficultySequencer.test.ts, difficultySequencer.variety.test.ts) continue to pass; determinism is preserved (no randomness).
- JSDoc documents the enforcement approach and the rules-wins-over-target precedence.
- UK English in comments/docs.

## Key Files
- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts
- src/core/waveBalance.ts (from F2)
- src/core/difficultySequencer.test.ts
- src/core/difficultySequencer.variety.test.ts

# Live thruster config carried in BotSnapshot

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

`BotSnapshot` must carry the player's live thruster physics — forward
`thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration` and reverse
`enabled` / `reverseAcceleration` / `reverseMaxSpeed` — sourced from the live
`Player`/`ShipConfig` via `buildBotSnapshot`, not from tunables.

As a player who tuned my ship, I want the demo bot to receive my live thruster
configuration in its decision input, so the bot flies the same physics I
configured without any code edits.

## Scope

- Add a public `Player.getThrusterConfig()` getter returning the forward and
  reverse thruster physics, mirroring the existing `getRotationConfig()`
  precedent (reads the live/effective `_config`).
- Extend `BotPlayer` in `botSnapshot.ts` (nested `thruster` object or
  flattened fields) and populate it in `buildBotSnapshot` via the structural
  `BotPlayerSource` seam — only when the source exposes it, so snapshots from
  sources without the getter keep their existing shape.
- Ensure the derived `BotWorld.player` and the pure decision layer receive the
  config unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Player.getThrusterConfig()` returns forward thrust acceleration, max speed and friction deceleration, plus reverse enabled / acceleration / max speed, mirroring the `getRotationConfig()` precedent.
- `BotPlayer` carries the thruster physics and `buildBotSnapshot` populates it from the player source via the structural `BotPlayerSource` seam; when the source does not expose the config the field is omitted so existing fallback semantics hold.
- `BotWorld.player` and the pure decision layer receive the config unchanged from the snapshot (no re-derivation, no live game access inside steering).
- The existing demo path `PlayScene._advanceDemoBot` → `buildBotSnapshot(this)` picks the values up automatically, with no hard-coded physics in the decision layer; the `BotSnapshotScene`/`BotPlayerSource` seams are updated to match.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — `BotPlayer` thruster fields, `BotPlayerSource` seam, `buildBotSnapshot` wiring.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — new public `getThrusterConfig()` getter.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — confirm `BotWorld.player` carries the config unchanged.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.test.ts` — builder tests for the new fields and the absent-config path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — verify the demo path consumes the snapshot without other hard-coded thruster use.

## Dependencies

- Depends on AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9's test-harness child (test-first baseline).

## Out of scope

- The steering/forward-model consumption of these values (next child).
- `assumedBulletSpeed` / `firePredictionHorizon` (enemy-bullet modelling).

## References

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` (`thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration`, `asteroidsReverse*`)

# Steering and forward model consume live thruster values

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

The steering candidate prediction (`evaluateDirection` player-speed term) and
the forward-model thrust decision (`mayThrust` friction stopping distance) must
use the snapshot's live values; the tunables `playerSpeed` /
`frictionDeceleration` become **defaults/overrides**, never authoritative.

As a designer editing `frictionDeceleration`/`maxSpeed`, I want the demo bot's
steering and stopping behaviour to track the change without code edits, so I
can validate tuning in a gym or a run.

## Scope

- `evaluateDirection`: use the snapshot's live max speed for the candidate
  speed term, falling back to tunables `playerSpeed`.
- `mayThrust`: use the snapshot's live friction deceleration for stopping
  distance, falling back to tunables `frictionDeceleration`.
- Precedence: explicit `GymBotTuning` override > live `ShipConfig` > compiled
  tunable default.
- Preserve exact default-equivalence: with no config present the decisions are
  bit-for-bit unchanged vs today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `evaluateDirection`'s candidate-speed term uses the snapshot's live max speed when present, falling back to the `playerSpeed` tunable otherwise.
- `mayThrust` computes stopping distance with the snapshot's live friction deceleration when present, falling back to the `frictionDeceleration` tunable; explicit GymBotTuning overrides still win over live config, which wins over the compiled default (documented precedence).
- With no config in the snapshot the decisions are bit-for-bit identical to today's `playerSpeed: 175` / `frictionDeceleration: 100` constants (default-equivalence preserved).
- At least one unit test pins a pure decision consuming live values and changing the outcome versus the defaults; the fallback-path baseline test stays green.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection`, `mayThrust`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — `playerSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration` documented as defaults/overrides.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — world view carries the player config (if the term is read from the world).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts` — custom-vs-default and fallback tests.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.test.ts` — end-to-end decision coverage.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the BotSnapshot thruster-config child (AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9).
- Depends on the test-harness child.

## Out of scope

- Reverse thrust modelling (next child).
- Enemy-bullet fire-prediction tunables.

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9

# Reverse braking model consumes live reverse thruster values

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

Reverse braking must be gated and modelled with the live reverse values:
`asteroidsReverseEnabled` (already respected at snapshot level),
`asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` feed the
reverse forward-model instead of being absent.

As a player who re-tuned or disabled my reverse thruster, I want the bot's
reverse braking to use my configured acceleration and speed cap, so the demo
never contradicts the handling I experience.

## Scope

- Feed the live reverse acceleration and/or reverse speed cap into the reverse
  forward-model (brake distance under reverse acceleration and/or reverse
  speed cap).
- Keep the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`,
  `reverseRetreatRange`) as tunables.
- Preserve the trouble/correction semantics from AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 (reverse
  is not a general positioning tool).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reverse forward-model consumes `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and/or `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` from the snapshot to model reverse-assisted braking distance / reverse speed cap, instead of omitting reverse physics entirely.
- Reverse remains gated on the snapshot's live `reverseEnabled`, and the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`) remain tunables.
- The reverse-reserved-for-trouble/correction semantics of AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 are preserved (no reverse used for routine positioning).
- Unit tests cover a custom reverse config changing the reverse decision versus defaults, and reverse-disabled behaviour emitting no reverse.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `mayReverse` / reverse forward-model.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — reverse fields consumed.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — reverse gate/default docs.
